summary.title: Build Your Own Redis: Barebones TCP Server [1/4]
summary.one_liner: You learn how TCP differs from HTTP and how to write a minimal TCP server in Ruby that accepts client connections, the first step toward a toy Redis clone.
takeaways: TCP is a transport-layer byte stream with no built-in notion of requests or responses, unlike HTTP.
netcat and lsof can be used to observe listening and established TCP sockets on a port.
Ruby's TCPServer.new(port) and server.accept create a listening server and yield a client connection per call.
A RedisServer class can wrap a TCPServer and loop on accept; serving clients is left for the next article.
summary.summary: This first article in a four-part series introduces TCP as a byte-oriented transport layer beneath application protocols like HTTP. It demonstrates the idea hands-on with netcat for client and server, and uses lsof to show LISTEN and ESTABLISHED socket states. It then builds a minimal TCP server in Ruby using TCPServer and accept, wrapped in a RedisServer class that loops on accepting clients without yet replying to them.
